exposure: Maternal serum 25(OH)-vitamin D levels during the second trimester of pregnancy
maternal serum 25(OH)-vitamin D levels during the second trimester of pregnancy
Serum Vitamin D quartiles (>30, 30-49, 50-74 and >75 nmol/L)
outcome: Infantile outcomes (birth weight, body length, and head circumference)
cohort: 890 pregnant women from the Western Australian Pregnancy Cohort (Raine) study
finding: Low maternal serum levels of 25(OH)-vitamin D during the second trimester are associated with an increased risk of gestational diabetes, potentially modified by race/ethnicity, while high pre-gestational BMI is a predictor of GDM risk, and GDM may increase the risk of caesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Women with GDM were at a greater risk of primary caesarean delivery.
birth_weight: Mentioned, but specific values not provided
